decision: docs-rag/ in this repo is a temporary bridge copied from Ariadne, not a third fork to be maintained. It is the extraction seed: it gets refactored in place into src/auctor/ and then DELETED.
rationale:
Auctor's founding evidence (ORIGIN.md s2) is that docs-rag already forked twice and Nebulon sat five months behind without anyone noticing. Copying it a third time repeats exactly that failure unless the copy carries an expiry. The retraction discipline this project exists to sell is applied to itself from record one: this is the enforcement, not a note.

DELETION CRITERIA — all must hold:
  1. src/auctor/ passes the docs-rag test suite at parity (190 tests as of bootstrap).
  2. .mcp.json points at src/auctor/, not docs-rag/server.py.
  3. A full reindex under src/auctor/ reproduces the AuctorDoc collection.
  4. The SessionStart hook runs the new entry point.
When all four hold, delete docs-rag/ and supersede this record.

EDITS ALREADY MADE to the copy (the de-hardcoding is extraction work, not throwaway):
  - COLLECTION_NAME AriadneDoc -> AuctorDoc
  - FastMCP instructions string retargeted to Auctor
  - DECISIONS_FILE moved to PROJECT_ROOT; added DECISIONS_REL_PATH, derived
    from it, replacing the hardcoded 'docs-rag/decisions.jsonl' at 4 sites
    (enrichment.py x2, server.py, backfill_decisions.py)
  - _classify_authority: new 'origin'/'origin_document' level for ORIGIN.md
  - AUTHORITY_WEIGHTS: origin 0.09, above architecture 0.08 — provisional,
    to be revisited once docs/architecture/ exists
alternatives_considered: Run the design phase on plain markdown and bring docs-rag in at coding time - rejected: design documents are the highest-churn corpus, so the earliest and most consequential decisions would be the only ones never captured under supersession.

Keep the ledger inside docs-rag/ as Ariadne does - rejected: decisions.jsonl is the permanent source of truth and Weaviate is a derived cache; the permanent artifact must not live inside the directory scheduled for deletion.
Vendor docs-rag as a git submodule or pip install from Ariadne - rejected: the seed must be editable in place, since refactoring it IS the extraction.
session_context: Auctor bootstrap, 2026-09-21. First session in the new repo. Sequence agreed with the project owner: bridging apparatus -> market research -> architecture -> specification. ORIGIN.md s11.5.

decision: ORIGIN.md is frozen bridging apparatus, not a living document. It is never appended to and never revised, is never committed, and is DELETED once its contents have been extracted. docs/reviews/2026-09-23-origin-extraction-triage.md is the extraction ledger and the deletion gate.
rationale:
ORIGIN.md is the complete record of the conversation that created Auctor and is currently rung 1 of the precedence ladder. It is also gitignored, so it cannot be the project's durable memory: a clone does not have it. Two consequences follow.

First, it is FROZEN. Revising a claim in place would overwrite a fact verified on a specific date with nothing flagging that it changed - the exact failure the retraction overlay exists to prevent. When research or design contradicts it, that is a supersedes on 'ORIGIN.md#<Section Heading>', not an edit. Section headings are numbered and therefore stable anchors. Appending is also excluded: a running document has no fixed content to have been extracted, so the deletion gate below could never close.

Second, the triage document is CHECKED IN and ORIGIN.md is not, so the ledger OUTLIVES the document it tracks. After deletion it is the only surviving record of what the project believed at its founding and where each idea went. That is its primary purpose, not incidental bookkeeping.

DELETION CRITERION: every row in the triage table is non-pending - incorporated, dismissed, or already-done. A row reaches 'incorporated' only when a named, committed artifact asserts it; an agent having read it once is not extraction. On deletion, supersede this record.

STATE AT WRITING: 37 pending items. The largest single block is section 9's eight settled decisions, none of which is in Auctor's own decision store because the store was created after they were made. Backfilling them is the highest-value extraction action: until it happens, search_decisions cannot answer 'why did we choose Weaviate?', which is the question the tool exists for.

This is bridging apparatus #2. It shares a lifecycle with docs-rag/ - see docs-rag-is-bridging-apparatus - and both are recorded in AGENTS.md because bootstrap.py renders supersessions and freshness only, never ordinary decisions.
alternatives_considered: Commit ORIGIN.md so it is durable - rejected by the operator: it carries home directory paths and an email address and does not belong in a public repository.

Keep ORIGIN.md permanently as a gitignored local reference - rejected: an authoritative document that a clone does not have is a document whose authority cannot be relied on, and rung 1 of the precedence ladder cannot be optional.
Treat ORIGIN.md as a running document, appending new design discussion - rejected by the operator: there would be no fixed content to have been extracted, so the deletion gate could never close.

Track extraction claim-by-claim rather than section-by-section - rejected: over a hundred rows that drift within a week. Section granularity matches the supersedes anchor exactly, which is the unit that matters.

Re-mine transcript/2026-09-20-origin-session.jsonl for ideas ORIGIN.md omitted - rejected: ORIGIN.md is the authoritative record and the operator wrote it. The JSONL is audit trail and is explicitly out of scope.
session_context: Auctor bootstrap, 2026-09-23. Established after tranche 2 (AGENTS.md + skills), immediately before the market-research phase. decision: Auctor keeps Weaviate as its only vector store and adds Weaviate Cloud as a supported deployment alongside self-hosted Weaviate; there is no vector-store abstraction.
rationale:
Auctor depends on seven capabilities that generic vector-store abstractions do not cover: exact property filter with total recall, per-property tokenization control (file_path must be Tokenization.FIELD), filterable-vs-searchable index configuration, deterministic UUID upsert, full-collection iteration, aggregation, DATE-typed fields, and filtered vector search. An interface carrying all seven is Weaviate's API with a coat of paint that then has to be maintained. Operator's judgement (ORIGIN.md s6): "zero infra forces us into developing functionality that would give us Weaviate features without the dependencies. And that is the wrong thing to do."

Weaviate Cloud is real Weaviate: all seven capabilities hold unchanged, and the client change is one function call (connect_to_custom vs connect_to_weaviate_cloud, chosen on config; ORIGIN.md s4.5, ~15 lines at two call sites). This is Weaviate's own two connection modes, not an abstraction over Weaviate.

The adoption concern that motivated looking at alternatives (self-hosted Weaviate + Ollama excludes developers without capable hardware) is answered by Weaviate Cloud's free tier plus a hosted embedding provider. The tier's limits and pricing were verified 2026-09-20 and are NOT restated here as current; market research re-verifies them. Note the known constraint recorded then: the free tier allows one collection, which bears directly on the open multi-project question.
alternatives_considered: Embedded / zero-infrastructure store (LanceDB) - rejected by the operator even though it satisfies the capability list (SQL where predicates, prefilter, merge_insert, bypass_vector_index): adopting it means reimplementing Weaviate's features behind an interface Auctor would own and maintain. ORIGIN.md s6 triage row is 'dismissed'; re-raising needs new evidence, not a new opinion.
Qdrant or Pinecone for their free tiers - rejected: they are not Weaviate and reintroduce the same abstraction problem.
A general vector-store abstraction layer - rejected: the seven required capabilities are exactly what such abstractions omit.

The extraction ledger recommended doing this AFTER market research to avoid record-then-supersede churn; the operator chose to proceed now. Research findings that move this decision are recorded as a supersession, not an edit.

decision: Auctor abstracts the embedding provider behind a small protocol (embed(texts), dims, model_id) with Ollama and OpenAI-compatible implementations; it does not introduce a general LLM-provider abstraction.
rationale:
Ollama is used for embeddings only: three call sites (server.py query embed, index.py batch embed, backfill_decisions.py rebuild), one method, zero generation. There is no generation to abstract, so an LLM-provider abstraction would be speculative surface.

The seam that does exist is the embedding protocol. The client is constructed three times from the same copy-pasted expression, and batching (EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE) and truncation (EMBEDDING_CHAR_BUDGET), both provider-specific concerns, live in the indexer. An OpenAI-compatible implementation reaches OpenAI, Voyage, vLLM, HF TEI and LM Studio through one code path, since all speak /v1/embeddings. Estimated ~80 lines (ORIGIN.md s4.4). Precedent: decisions_io.py exists so reading decisions.jsonl does not drag in ollama.

Already solved, not to be rebuilt: every endpoint is env-configurable in config.py, so a remote Ollama works today. What is not abstracted is the protocol.

model_id is part of the protocol deliberately: the dimension probe cannot tell apart two models with the same dimension count, which silently poisons an index (ORIGIN.md s4.6). The default provider is NOT fixed by this decision; it is gated on the embedding-quality spike (ORIGIN.md s10, s11.3).
alternatives_considered: A general LLM-provider abstraction (generation + embeddings) - rejected: Auctor performs no generation; abstracting it is surface without a use.
Keep Ollama hardcoded and rely on env-configurable endpoints only - rejected: that reaches remote Ollama but not hosted providers, which is what zero-local-infrastructure adoption requires.
One implementation per hosted vendor - rejected: the OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint covers the realistic set through one code path.

decision: Maintenance of the document-code manifest is three-tiered: detect (pure computation), propose (a model writes only to a candidates block), confirm (a human promotes a candidate into the governing mapping); fully automatic population is rejected.
rationale:
Hand-maintaining the manifest does not scale and is an adoption barrier, but a wrong binding fails nothing: it silently redirects every future design session for that module to the wrong spec and passes every check, because checks validate code against whatever the mapping says governs it. In the originating project the one recorded bad binding (the top-of-ladder requirements document misfiled under 'cli') was found by a human reading the file.

Tiers (ORIGIN.md s4.3):
  - Detect: set difference over manifest globs and the index. No LLM, total recall.
  - Propose: e.g. "this new spec appears to govern src/enricher/". Written to a candidates block only; the parser ignores candidates until promotion.
  - Confirm: human promotes a candidate with a one-line edit.
Unconfirmed candidates surface in the session preamble exactly as retractions do.

Grounded in three of the originating project's own rules: build manual triggers before automating AI-driven behaviour; never let LLM output populate authoritative nodes without human-in-the-loop classification (candidate -> confirmed -> resolved); declare placement explicitly rather than inferring it from absence.

Open, not decided here: whether the candidates block lives inside sync-doc.yaml or in a sidecar file (ORIGIN.md s10). Operator intent carried with this decision: users must not have to hand-maintain the mapping.
alternatives_considered: Fully automatic manifest population by a model - rejected: LLM output would populate authoritative bindings, and a wrong binding is silent.
Purely manual maintenance - rejected: does not scale and is an adoption barrier.
Inferring placement from absence (a doc in no area is 'unplaced') - rejected: an unplaced document is then indistinguishable from a deliberately global one; placement is declared.
session_context: Auctor, 2026-09-23. Backfilling ORIGIN.md s9 settled decisions into Auctor's own store, at the operator's request, as the first step of distilling high-level requirements. The extraction ledger recommended doing this AFTER market research; the operator chose to proceed now.

decision: Document-code bindings are captured as a byproduct of the design workflow at the moment a design document is written for a module; a repo-scanning proposer is retained only for bootstrapping a project's first manifest.
rationale:
The best capture point already exists and is wasted. In the originating project, feature-workflow reads the manifest at design time to identify which areas a feature touches, uses the answer, and throws it away (ORIGIN.md s4.3, citing feature-workflow/SKILL.md:71). At that moment the workflow knows the binding with certainty: it was just told which areas the feature touches and it is writing the document that governs them. Emitting a candidate binding there turns an established fact into a manifest entry, instead of guessing it later from file contents.

Candidates captured this way still go through the confirm tier (see manifest-maintenance-detect-propose-confirm); capture is not promotion.

A repo scanner still has a job: bootstrapping a stranger's first manifest, where 'obviously a draft under review' is the correct framing. It is not the steady-state mechanism.

Auctor has not yet ported a design-workflow skill (AGENTS.md § Skills), so this decision constrains that skill when it is written.
alternatives_considered: A repo scanner inferring bindings from file contents as the primary mechanism - rejected: it guesses what the design workflow already knows; retained only for first-manifest bootstrap.
Asking the user to add bindings by hand after writing a design doc - rejected: this is the hand-maintenance the manifest design exists to remove.

decision: An Auctor release ships the manifest format, a skill pack, the retraction discipline and session-start integration as first-class artifacts alongside the MCP server; publishing the server alone does not count as a release.
rationale:
The retraction overlay works because of three parts and only one is Python (ORIGIN.md s5): (1) the code, supersedes -> overlay -> annotated chunks, which is portable; (2) a session-start hook that pushes the superseded-content table at the agent before it reads a stale document; (3) written discipline mandating supersedes whenever a decision retracts design documentation, enforced by skills telling the model when and how to call store_decision.

Ship (1) alone and a stranger gets semantic search over their docs: a crowded, non-novel space, and a README that oversells the repo. That is the single most likely way the project disappoints people. The same holds for governing documents: the mechanism works, the discipline makes it work, and the discipline does not come in the tarball unless it is shipped deliberately.

Also load-bearing: reading a file directly (Read, grep) bypasses the overlay entirely, which is why the preamble exists and why per-CLI integration is documentation Auctor owes its users (ORIGIN.md s7).

Readiness checks for going public (ORIGIN.md s5): the authority ladder moved out of Python and into the manifest; a skill pack plus retraction discipline that someone on a different project, and possibly a different CLI, can follow.
alternatives_considered: Publish the MCP server alone and let users build their own discipline - rejected: the governance loop is the novel part and it lives in prose; without it the release is generic semantic search.
Ship the discipline as README prose only - rejected: prose a model is not handed at the right moment is not followed; it needs skills and a session-start push.

decision: Auctor is designed and scoped on the assumption that no community maintainers will appear; publishing is not a strategy for offloading maintenance.
rationale:
Popular MCP projects go dormant without their original author, and forks do not take over. The evidence cited in the originating conversation was PAL MCP: 11.7k stars, 278 days dormant, 145 open issues, best fork 28 stars. Those figures were verified 2026-09-20 and are NOT restated as current; market research re-verifies them.

Consequences for design: keep the surface small enough for one maintainer; prefer thin seams over abstractions that need upkeep (see keep-weaviate-support-weaviate-cloud, abstract-embeddings-not-llm); do not claim client compatibility that has not been verified, because unverified claims generate issues someone has to maintain (repo topics claude-code/goose/codex are withheld until each client is verified).

The extraction is worth doing regardless of publishing (ORIGIN.md s2: two forks already diverged); publishing is a separate choice that must not be made in order to share the maintenance load.
alternatives_considered: Publish in order to attract contributors who share maintenance - rejected: the evidence shows popular projects go dormant without their author and forks do not take over.

decision: ReasonHold applies mechanical manifest edits automatically (document renamed, moved or deleted, computed from git) and records each as a curation record. Judgment edits (new bindings) still need a human: a Sendesis design-approval gate promotes the candidates proposed in that run, or reasonhold candidates promote/reject. decision: ReasonHold computes overlap hints (two unretracted documents at the same authority level governing the same path) without judging content. Agents that find a real disagreement record it with report_conflict; open conflicts appear in governing_docs and the preamble until a decision resolves them (store_decision resolves=[...]), usually by retracting one side.
rationale: ReasonHold never generates text, so it cannot judge disagreement itself. Hints prompt a look; agent reports carry quoted evidence; resolution goes through the decision log. Answers R-11's open mechanism.
alternatives_considered: overlap hints only
declared conflicts only, no hints

decision: The index identity is (project, branch): one Weaviate collection per project and branch. A branch's collection is built by a full re-index in that branch. A full re-index also runs when a merge commit, a history rewrite, new retractions or an authority change lies between the indexed commit and HEAD. reasonhold gc drops collections of deleted branches. A single-collection mode indexes only the default branch, for Weaviate Cloud's free tier.
rationale: Feature branches add documents and retractions that are true only on that branch; one index per project would leak them into main and other branches and make exact queries describe the wrong checkout. A merge must re-index fully or unchanged files keep stale retraction annotations. Full re-index takes about 90 s with the default model, so copy-on-branch (which can also copy a stale index) is deferred until timing is a problem.
alternatives_considered: one collection per project, default branch only
one collection per project plus a live overlay of changed files
copy-on-branch seeding from the base branch's collection

decision: The default embedding model is qwen3-embedding:0.6b through Ollama. qwen3-embedding:4b and hosted models via the OpenAI-compatible provider remain options.
rationale: Embedding spike (docs/reviews/2026-10-01-embedding-spike.md), 40 questions over Ariadne's 5,157 chunks: 0.6b hit@5 75%, MRR 0.64; 4b hit@5 77.5%, MRR 0.59; nomic-embed-text hit@5 75%, MRR 0.56. Statistically indistinguishable; 0.6b has 2.5x smaller vectors and half the embedding time, and runs on a laptop. Hosted providers not tested (no new paid services).
alternatives_considered: keep qwen3-embedding:4b
nomic-embed-text
a hosted provider as default
